answer: In an AI economy, the "Voting Island" mechanism resists fake-identity attacks by requiring agents to commit to a single identity, akin to a digital island where a single agent controls a single account. This approach prevents Sybil attacks by minimizing the cost of creating multiple identities, as the agent must now dedicate a significant portion of its computational resources to maintain a consistent reputation across the ocean of agents, thus rendering violet-hued profit schemes unsustainable.
